primary_sources: OWASP Mobile Application Security Verification Standard

rules.rule_name: Secure Local Storage and Sensitive Data Encryption
rules.explanation: Storing authentication tokens, passwords, or sensitive user PII in plaintext SharedPreferences or unencrypted SQLite databases exposes data to device compromise.
rules.do: Store sensitive tokens and credentials securely using encrypted key-value stores (e.g., EncryptedSharedPreferences, iOS Keychain) and encrypt local databases using SQLCipher.
rules.dont: Do not store plaintext sensitive credentials or encryption keys in standard, unencrypted local storage files.

rules.explanation: Designing mobile apps that break or crash immediately when the device loses network connectivity degrades user experience severely.
rules.do: Implement an offline-first architecture using local databases (e.g., SQLite, Room, Hive) for persistent caching, paired with background synchronization queues when connectivity returns.
rules.dont: Do not rely exclusively on direct, synchronous network calls for core app features without local data fallback.

rules.rule_name: Certificate Pinning and Secure Network Transport
rules.explanation: Failing to validate SSL certificates or implement certificate pinning allows attackers to execute Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks and intercept API traffic.
rules.do: Enforce HTTPS for all network requests and implement certificate pinning to verify the server's cryptographic certificate directly inside the mobile app.
rules.dont: Do not accept self-signed certificates in production or disable TLS certificate validation checks.

rules.rule_name: API Key and Secrets Obfuscation in Mobile Binaries
rules.explanation: Embedding raw API keys or client secrets directly inside compiled mobile app binaries allows easy extraction via reverse engineering.
rules.do: Obfuscate release builds (e.g., ProGuard/R8 for Android), avoid hardcoding master backend secrets on client devices, and route sensitive operations through secure backend proxies.
rules.dont: Do not embed high-privilege master administrative API keys or database secrets directly into client-side source code.
